answer: Each new identity locks a timber of scarce collateral that unfreezes only after several epochs of unique, peer-replayed work. Those traces form a public trellis: every claim needs K independent co-signers who match-stake the same sum and lose it if the identity is later proven cloned. A falcon auditor samples random clusters each epoch and compares cadence, wording fingerprints, and commitment hashes. Collisions slash the cluster and pay detectors. An attacker must fund a fresh lock per fake account, buy K co-signers who risk slashing, and cannot reuse generation patterns as sybils grow.
